findings.text: Controller context keeps distributor and CPU base selectors, raw mappings, per CPU offset, saved shared state arrays, per CPU saved private pointers, owning domain and interrupt count. Base selector offers either a shared mapping or a per CPU table.

One configuration guards map updates with a shared raw spin guard in both interrupt saving and plain forms. An alternate configuration provides the same four operations as empty macros that discard flags.
Directly tracked CPU interface limit is 8.

Software generated numbers lie below 16, private numbers below 32, shared numbers from 32 upward. Top level acknowledge loop stops at or above 1020; cascaded path treats its spurious encoding as no work.
CPU priority width accepts 4 or 5 with fallback to 4 on unexpected encoding; identifier width accepts 16 or 24 with fallback to 16. Effective width is the smaller nonzero of CPU and routing values.

Private domain always created linear; shared domain only when count nonzero; processor messaging domain only when message parent exists, sized by per CPU count times possible CPUs. Any creation failure releases all domains already made.

Virtualization setup stops quietly when capability flag clear. When capable, firmware maintenance interrupt must be nonzero or setup warns and stops; otherwise version marker and maintenance data are registered. Alternate build provides empty setup.

Common bring up establishes domains and interface widths before starting current CPU, installing top handler and enabling routing and multiprocessor and message facilities. Failures unwind by clearing handler, disabling CPU interrupts and freeing domains.

Firmware tree entry probes routing, runs common bring up and configures virtualization, removing routing on failure. Firmware table entry performs single global handle allocation, probes routing, runs common bring up and installs model callbacks, releasing handle and routing on failure.

Table acceptance requires version equality with expected driver data. Signal translation sends bridge typed signals to interconnect handles and all other signals to the single global domain or null handle form.
Base resolution uses per CPU table when variant flag enabled and shared mapping otherwise. Alternate build always uses shared mapping with empty enable.
Presence of handler private data marks a cascaded secondary that cannot be forwarded. Forwarding control also rejects software generated numbers and otherwise toggles forwarded state.

Masking disables and unmasking enables. One completion mode always signals completion; the other suppresses deactivation for forwarded interrupts and also clears active on mask to prevent stuck state. Software generated completions reuse stashed acknowledge encoding.
Pending and active controls follow requested boolean directly; masked control is inverted relative to enable. Unsupported state selectors fail.
Software generated configuration accepts only rising edge. Shared configuration accepts only high level or rising edge. Private misconfiguration warns but is treated as success.

Top handler drains acknowledge values until terminator, completes when deactivation supported, orders memory for software generated numbers, stashes their encoding per CPU and dispatches each number to the primary domain.
Cascaded handler brackets a single acknowledge and dispatch with chained enter and exit, skipping spurious encoding and invoking bad interrupt handling on dispatch failure.
Chained entry does nothing for completion capable parents and otherwise masks with acknowledgement; chained exit completes when capable and otherwise unmasks.
External use can bind a secondary controller as chained handler with index bound check, and can power down a CPU interface with index validation by clearing its enable.

Power control can save and restore distributor configuration, targeting, enable and active state, and per CPU private enable, active and configuration state, guarding null context and missing mappings.

Distributor setup disables, retargets shared interrupts to the boot CPU, applies default priority and reenables. CPU setup validates index, records mask for primary while clearing it from peers, programs private defaults and threshold, then enables interface preserving bypass bits.
Second generation CPU interface is detected by masked identifier match. Bring up clears its active priority storage and enables split completion mode only for primary when deactivation supported.

Out of range CPU, missing CPU mask on multiprocessor, missing maintenance interrupt, missing message parent, null save context and unexpected newer CPU interface each warn or taint; controller index overflow traps.
Single per CPU slot for software generated acknowledge assumes no nesting; spurious acknowledge must be ignored rather than dispatched.
Diagnostics show firmware node name when power device present, else controller index derived from table position.
Virtualization record uses version five marker with maintenance interrupt from firmware cell zero and cleared mask flag.
Retrigger asserts pending state and signals success with nonzero.

Deactivation support defaults enabled, Franken variant and read modify write need default disabled; feature check warns once with taint on unexpected newer interface, with alternate build as no operation.
Version two virtualization record is reserved in init memory.
Distributor and CPU mappings for an interrupt are obtained from its chip context through variant aware selection.
